trial.ground_truth: Payment delays 3 seconds while caller timeout is 2 seconds
trial.predicted_root_cause: payment-service /charge is systematically slow (~3006ms p50, all 200s) while order-service applies an ~2000ms HTTP client read timeout. The order-service→payment-service client span in the trace is marked ERROR with otel.status_description "ReadTimeout" and duration 2005464us (~2.0s). order-service therefore returns 502 at ~2018ms (94% error rate) and gateway, which calls order-service, mirrors the 502 at ~2014ms (48.5% error rate). evidence: order-service /checkout logs (E-65e08d5269324712) show 502 at ~2018ms; payment-service /charge logs (E-fdc455374dca4da3) show status 200 at ~3006ms; trace (E-c7723a8f9d714058, E-1d39c47c4fd74df7) shows client span error=true / ReadTimeout ~2s. DB pool stats for order-service and payment-service are healthy (pool_available=3, requests_waiting=0), Kafka consumer lag is 0, and inventory/user/notification services are fast and healthy (E-76270a9715f34dc0, E-a1d88e45f2b24c1e, E-46e36e63520346aa). The order/payment pools show no exhaustion or queueing, ruling out DB_POOL_EXHAUSTION and DATABASE_SLOW_QUERY for this symptom.

regression_risks: Raising the order-service HTTP client read timeout beyond ~3s would mask a genuine downstream slowdown and propagate ~3s latency upstream, degrading gateway user-visible latency.
A circuit breaker/fallback added without bounded timeouts could cause partial-order state or duplicate charge attempts.
Any change touching services/pricing.py would risk breaking the immutable pricing contract tests without addressing the timeout.
critic_result.test_sufficiency: Sufficient for diagnosis verification only. Three independent evidence classes (HTTP logs sharing trace_ids, before/after metrics, distributed trace) converge on caller-timeout-vs-slow-callee, with healthy pools/lag ruling out common alternatives. No patch applied (NO_CODE_PATCH), so no regression or recovery test exists to evaluate. The pg_sleep statements corroborate injected latency but the exact payment-service internal cause remains unverified and outside allowlisted scope.
critic_result.verification_summary: The diagnosis is supported by convergent, independently-typed evidence. HTTP logs (E-65e08d5269324712, E-fdc455374dca4da3) show order-service /checkout returning 502 at ~2018ms while payment-service /charge completes 200 at ~3006ms across shared trace_ids, and gateway mirrors the 502 at ~2014ms. Metrics reproduce this: before-window order-service p50 2018ms with 94-100% errors vs payment-service p50 3006ms with 0% errors (E-9e64de9fd74742ae); the after-window shows order-service 0.00% errors and p50 5.28ms (E-6101c4986e284687). The trace (E-1d39c47c4fd74df7) shows the order-to-payment client span failing with a 502/error internal span. Healthy DB pools (available=3, waiting=0) and zero Kafka lag (E-76270a9715f34dc0, E-a1d88e45f2b24c1e) rule out pool exhaustion and consumer lag. The DB statements view shows 'SELECT pg_sleep' with mean_exec_time 2001.7ms (488 calls) and 1202ms (460 calls) (E-f11fb9f9c9e74c99), corroborating an injected-latency mechanism consistent with the ~2s/3s pattern. Allowlisted targets (pricing.py contract E-7d4f7949eee2408c; runtime.py fault() reading a Redis 'fault:' key E-40cbf2e2a4d240dc) contain no timeout or payment logic, confirming NO_CODE_PATCH. Verification covers diagnosis only, not remediation; operator restoration is observational and not an AI patch or proof of a unique mechanism.
alternative_explanations: Latency may be a generic injected/scheduled fault (pg_sleep ~2001ms and ~1202ms; Redis 'fault:' flag) rather than a specific payment-service defect — the exact injection target cannot be resolved from allowlisted source.
The ~2000ms read-timeout value is inferred from the failing span and 502 wall time; the literal order-service HTTP client timeout constant is not visible in allowlisted source.
Operator restoration removing the error is not definitive proof of a unique mechanism, since fault removal could independently explain recovery.

Evidence is strong across two independent sources: HTTP logs showing payment 3006ms/200 vs order 502 at ~2018ms, and traces showing the client span ERROR with ReadTimeout ~2005ms. Confirmed by metrics (payment p50 3006ms 0% errors, order p50 2018ms ~95-100% errors) and healthy DB pools/Kafka lag ruling out alternatives. The general mechanism is materially correct even without the exact injection implementation detail (Redis fault flag), which is acceptable.
